new_packages.label_en: Corruption of Speech and Exile of the Divine Presence
new_packages.reason: Torah #58 sections ט–י contain a tightly structured evil-domain cluster that mirrors Package 2 (Greatness/Malkhut/Shechina) precisely. The Torah explicitly states (line 28): 'גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה, הַיְנוּ הַגְּדֻלָּה, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מַלְכוּת, בְּחִינַת שְׁכִינָה, נִפְגָּם וְנַעֲשֶׂה גַּאֲוָה' — the same malkhut/shechina/greatness of Package 2, when damaged by speech corruption, becomes pride/gaava and exile of the Shechina. This is the structural evil mirror of Package 2. The evil cluster has at least four explicitly named concepts with bechina language: (1) 'בַּבְלִיִּים, הַיְנוּ הַדּוֹר הַפּוֹגְמִים בְּהַדִּבּוּר' — Babylonians = those who corrupt speech (line 30); (2) 'גַּאֲוָה' — pride as the result of corrupted malkhut (line 27: 'נִלְכָּדִים בַּעֲוֹן גַּאֲוָה'); (3) 'גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה' — exile of the Shechina (line 28); (4) 'סֶגֹּל גָּלוּת' — 'the exile-segol' as bechina of the hod/malkhut in their fallen state (line 32). These form an independent evil domain not covered by the three existing packages. None appear as bechina-connected nodes in the dataset for Torah #58, but all have explicit bechina language in the source text and form a coherent thematic cluster constituting the exact evil counterpart to Package 2's holy malkhut.

new_packages.mirror_explanation: Package 2 (גְּדֻלָּה/מַלְכוּת/שְׁכִינָה) describes the holy state: when Shabbat illumination flows properly, the 'proper ones of the generation' receive beauty and greatness (גדולה = sign of Torah). This new evil package describes the exact fallen mirror: when the generation corrupts its speech (בבליים), the Shabbat-light cannot flow, the holiness of malkhut/shechina is damaged, and the greatness turns into pride (גאוה) — exile of the Shechina (גלות השכינה). Same nodes, opposite orientation: גדולה becomes גאוה, מלכות becomes גלות השכינה, holy sign (סגל) becomes exile-segol.

observations:
Torah #58 has the classic good/evil mirror structure identified in the framework. The three positive packages (Patriarchal Gifts, Holy Malkhut, Shabbat/Teshuva) form the positive teaching. The evil mirror of Package 2 (Holy Malkhut/Shechina) is clearly articulated in the text's final sections as a distinct conceptual domain with at least 5 named concepts having explicit bechina or haynu-bechina language. This evil cluster is NOT represented in the current dataset at all — no bechina edges exist for these concepts in Torah #58. The proposed new package has 4+ concepts and 4 internal bechina relationships extractable from the source text, making it a well-formed new package candidate.

The evil mirror of Package 1 (Patriarchal Gifts) would be עֲמָלֵק — who defiled the Brit of the Patriarchs (line 6: 'עֲמָלֵק טִמֵּא בְּרִיתָם'). However, עמלק appears only as an agent described in narrative/eitza terms, without a distinct bechina cluster of 3+ nodes equating Amalek's nature to other concepts in Torah #58. A single-node evil concept (Amalek) does not qualify as a new package.

The evil mirror of Package 3 (Shabbat/Teshuva/Double Torah) would be those who cannot receive Shabbat at all. The text mentions this (line 35: 'שֶׁאֵין מְקַבְּלִין חִיּוּת שַׁבָּת') but without a cluster of bechina-parallel concepts; it is described causally (because of speech corruption), making it part of the Package 4 evil domain rather than a separate package.

The good/evil mirror structure in Torah #58:
  Package 1 (Patriarchs/Gifts) — positive → evil mirror: Amalek (defiler of covenant, insufficient for new package)
  Package 2 (Malkhut/Shechina) — positive → evil mirror: THIS NEW PACKAGE (exile of Shechina through speech corruption) [proposed as torah_58_new_1]
  Package 3 (Shabbat/Teshuva) — positive → evil mirror: absence of Shabbat vitality (described causally, no independent bechina cluster)

Conclusion: One new package is warranted — the evil mirror of Package 2.
